idea.title: Quibi: premium 10-minute shows made for phones

source.text: Quibi: premium 10-minute shows made for phones, $4.99 per month with ads or $7.99 without, launch country US. Score it as of 2020-03-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a funded media startup. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug quibi.

idea.problem: Premium TV-quality entertainment does not fit the short, in-between moments people spend on their phones
idea.customer: US smartphone users aged 18-34 who watch video in short idle moments (assumption: the brief names no segment)
idea.solution: Premium scripted and unscripted shows in episodes of about 10 minutes, made for phones
claims: $4.99 per month with ads or $7.99 without

context.budget: Funded media startup (about USD 1.4B raised by 2020-02 per VideoWeek)

assumptions: Scored as of 2020-03-01 with only evidence published on or before that date
Target customer US 18-34 mobile viewers (not stated in the brief)
Headless run: no questions asked; follow-ups written as assumptions

confidence.note: Raised by a pre-launch paid-intent poll and a dated churn benchmark for new SVODs; only 3 primary sources

gross_margin.note: About **65%** after a 30% App Store cut and delivery (estimate); content is a fixed $1B/year on top.

ltv_cac.note: LTV ~$70 vs CAC ~$60 even at the **7.5M** target: ~1.2; at half the target it falls to ~0.6 (estimate).

pricing_power.note: Free YouTube, TikTok and Snapchat set the anchor; analysts call **$5** the upper end of the sweet spot.

build_effort.note: App, Turnstyle tech and 175 shows are already built; launch set for **2020-04-06**.

skills_match.note: Katzenberg (DreamWorks) and Whitman (eBay, HP) have run studios and consumer tech at scale.

capital_needed.note: About **$1.4B** raised, yet Whitman says more is needed to reach break-even.

time_to_mvp.note: Launch is about **5 weeks** after the scoring date.

sales_cycle.note: Consumer app subscription: same-day purchase, ads already pre-sold.

channel_readiness.note: **$400-500M** marketing, Super Bowl ad, T-Mobile partner; but no owned audience yet.

search_demand.note: Brand unknown: Whitman says **no one has heard of Quibi**; Super Bowl coverage asks what it is.

trend.note: US mobile time passed TV in 2019 (**3:43 vs 3:35** a day, eMarketer).

willingness_to_pay.note: Only **39%** interested in paid mobile-first short shows; 47% have subscription fatigue.

free_alternatives.note: Free socials fill the same in-between moments: Snapchat alone has **218M** daily users (R5 cap 2).

competitor_density.note: Netflix 167M, Disney+ 26.5M, Apple TV+, Peacock (free tier), HBO Max all fight for the wallet.

differentiation.note: One real difference: Hollywood-grade shows cut for phones, with **Turnstyle** portrait/landscape.

legal_regulatory.note: No licence needed; Turnstyle is patent-pending, no public IP dispute by 2020-03-01.

platform_dependency.note: App-only: Apple and Google take **30%** of in-app subscriptions in year one.

market_risk.note: Unproven format: Go90, Vessel and YouTube paid originals all failed or retreated.

skills.note: Founders have long track records in film and consumer tech at scale.

assets.note: Hollywood talent network, **$150M** pre-sold ads, T-Mobile distribution deal.

interest.note: Katzenberg has pitched mobile short-form for years; a multi-decade media career.

som.reasoning: 38M heavy viewers x 2-4% conversion cited by Digiday sources (2019-06) = 0.8-1.5M

price.reasoning: $4.99 ad tier and $7.99 ad-free (TechCrunch, 2020-01) blended at ~60/40 = ~$6

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Assumption: new library-light SVOD with no habit; no pre-2020-03 benchmark found; 8%/month

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Midpoint of 2-4% conversion of heavy mobile viewers cited in Digiday (2019-06)

cac.reasoning: $450M 2020 marketing (Digiday, 2020-02, $400-500M) / 7.5M year-1 target subs (Light Reading, 2020-01) = $60; at half target $120

ltv_cac.reasoning: $70 / $60 = 1.17 at Quibi's own target; $70 / $120 = 0.58 at half the target

payback_months.reasoning: $60 CAC / $5.57 monthly gross profit incl. ads = 10.8 months

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: $1B year-1 content spend (Tubefilter, 2019-06) / 12 = $83.3M, before marketing and staff

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: $83.3M content / $5.57 gross profit per sub per month = ~15M subs, vs a 7.5M year-1 target

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: Launch 2020-04-06 (TechCrunch, 2020-01) minus scoring date 2020-03-01 = 5 weeks; ads pre-sold

verdict.launch_reason: Founder's choice; the largest SVOD market with a carrier launch partner (T-Mobile).
verdict.cheapest_test: 7-day pricing fake door: card-on-file pre-orders at $4.99 / $7.99 from $200k of social ads to US 18-34; need >= 2% of visitors.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 20 card-on-file pre-orders per 1,000 visitors (2%) by day 7 -> add a free tier before paid launch
Episode completion under 50% on free platforms by day 7 -> cut the slate by half
Fewer than 2M app downloads in the first 30 days after 2020-04-06 -> freeze new content commissioning

rescue.change: Sell through carrier bundles (T-Mobile, others) at a wholesale fee per subscriber instead of paid retail acquisition
rescue.why: Cuts CAC and fixes ltv_cac; sidesteps the 30% store cut on platform_dependency
rescue.requires: Carrier contracts beyond the undisclosed T-Mobile launch deal

rescue.change: Add a free ad-supported tier (like Peacock Free) and keep $4.99 / $7.99 as upgrades
rescue.why: Meets free_alternative head-on and lifts willingness_to_pay and search_demand via reach

rescue.change: Halve the year-1 slate and pilot 10 shows on free platforms before going exclusive
rescue.why: Cuts the $1B fixed cost behind capital_needed and break-even; tests market_risk cheaply

type_checks.note: Ads pre-sold at premium rates: $150M first-year inventory sold out to 10 brands ($15M+ each), six months before launch.
App-only service: Apple takes 30% of in-app subscriptions in year one, 15% after; reflected in platform_dependency 2.5.

narrative.answer: **PIVOT 60/100.** The team, money and ad pre-sales are real, but Quibi asks people to pay for minutes that **free apps** already fill; even at its own 7.5M target, revenue covers about half the $1B content bill.
tldr: Execution is strong: $1.4B raised, 175 shows built, $150M ads sold, launch in 5 weeks.
Demand to pay is weak: free YouTube, TikTok and Snapchat own the same moments; 39% interest in paid mobile shows.
Unit economics fail at any plausible scale: break-even needs ~15M subs vs a 7.5M year-1 target.

key_findings.title: Free apps already own the moment
key_findings.detail: Analysts say Quibi's rivals are **free** socials; Snapchat alone has 218M daily users and costs $0.

key_findings.title: Even the target loses money
key_findings.detail: 7.5M subs x ~$6 + ads is ~$57M/month against **$83M/month** of content alone (estimate).

key_findings.title: The graveyard is full and recent
key_findings.detail: Go90 lost an estimated **$658M** before closing in 2018; Vessel and YouTube paid originals also retreated.

narrative.recommendation: Do not launch paid-only: add a **free ad tier** and halve the slate before 2020-04-06, then gate further content on 30-day retention.
narrative.steelman: Phones passed TV in daily time, and Quibi brings Hollywood talent, $1.4B, a T-Mobile deal and **$150M** pre-sold ads: no mobile video entrant was ever this well equipped. The evidence backs execution, not willingness to pay.
narrative.lesson: Money buys content and reach, not a habit people will pay for when free fills the same minutes.

free_alternative.evidence: Analysts (Light Reading, 2020-01-15) say Quibi's real rivals are free Facebook, TikTok, Instagram and Snapchat; Snapchat alone had 218M daily users in Q4 2019.

strong_competitor.evidence: Netflix 167M paid subs (Q4 2019), Disney+ 26.5M in seven weeks, YouTube Premium/Music 20M+, plus Apple TV+ at $4.99 and Peacock with a free tier.

graveyard.evidence: Verizon's Go90 lost an estimated $658M and shut in 2018; Vessel raised $130M+ and was shut in 2016; YouTube moved paid originals to free in 2019.

no_distribution.evidence: Clear: $400-500M 2020 marketing budget, Super Bowl and Oscars ads, and T-Mobile as launch partner give a channel; cost per subscriber is the issue, not reach.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Clear on variable cost: ~65% after the 30% App Store cut (estimate). The $1B content slate is fixed and shows up in break-even (~15M subs) instead.

weak_demand.evidence: Clear on trend: US mobile time passed TV in 2019 (eMarketer). Willingness to pay is the weak point (39% interested, Hub), scored in willingness_to_pay.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Clear: no licence needed and no public IP dispute by 2020-03-01 (Turnstyle patent-pending); app-store dependency is scored in platform_dependency.

saturated_wave.evidence: 5 major paid streaming launches (Apple TV+, Disney+, Quibi, Peacock, HBO Max) from 2019-11 to 2020-07, but none phone-only short-form: under the 10 near-identical threshold.

fact_checks.claim: $4.99 per month with ads or $7.99 without
fact_checks.evidence: Confirmed at CES 2020: $4.99 with ads, $7.99 without, launching April 6.
Pitched as the first streaming service designed exclusively for mobile, at about $100k per minute.

customer.segment: US 18-34 smartphone users watching 40+ minutes of mobile video a day in in-between moments (commute, queues)
customer.pain: Idle minutes on the phone; long-form TV doesn't fit them
customer.today: Free YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram; Netflix on the phone ~10% of the time

competitors.name: Snapchat (Discover, Snap Originals)
competitors.gap: Short shows but lower production value

competitors.name: Netflix
competitors.gap: Long-form, TV-first; ~10% of viewing on phones

competitors.name: Disney+
competitors.traction_note: 26.5M subscribers within seven weeks of launch

competitors.name: Apple TV+
competitors.traction_note: Free year with new Apple devices; subscribers undisclosed
competitors.gap: Same price as Quibi's ad tier, full-length shows

competitors.name: Peacock (NBCUniversal)
competitors.traction_note: Free to ~24M Comcast/Cox customers at launch (2020-04)

scenarios.name: Pessimistic
scenarios.note: 1M subs (Digiday 2-4% funnel) x $6 + $12.5M ads; costs = $83.3M content + $37.5M marketing + $1.8M store fees

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: Quibi's own 7.5M year-1 target; still ~$77M/month loss (estimate)

risks.risk: Low trial-to-paid conversion against free socials
Advertiser make-goods if audience guarantees are missed
Capital runs out before break-even (~15M subs)
risks.mitigation: Halve content spend; tie commissioning to retention

test_plan.step: Launch a pricing fake door: quibi.com waitlist showing $4.99 / $7.99 with card-on-file pre-order, 3 trailers
Spend $200k on TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram ads at US 18-34, split by price
Release 2 full episodes free on YouTube and Snapchat; compare completion vs native shorts
Count card-on-file pre-orders per 1,000 landing visitors and per price

changes.what: US mobile time passed TV time in 2019 (3:43 vs 3:35 a day).
Quibi sold out $150M of first-year ads six months before launch.
T-Mobile signed as exclusive mobile launch partner, terms undisclosed.
Disney+ and Apple TV+ launched in November 2019, crowding the subscription wallet.
Peacock announced a free ad-supported tier, setting a $0 anchor for premium streaming.

why_now.note: Phones won the attention, but **free socials** already fill those minutes and five paid launches crowd the wallet: the window is closing.

icp.who: US 18-34 smartphone users watching 40+ minutes of mobile video a day in in-between moments (commute, queues)
icp.pays_for_today: Netflix $8.99-15.99/month or nothing (YouTube, TikTok and Snapchat are free); 3 streaming services per household on average
icp.budget: About $5/month incremental at most (Strategy Analytics via VideoWeek, 2020-02)
icp.trigger: A few idle minutes on the phone: commuting, waiting in line

premortem.cause: Trial users don't convert: free YouTube, TikTok and Snapchat already fill the same idle minutes at $0.
premortem.early_signal: Under 20% of first-month users still watching weekly; daily viewing under 10 minutes

premortem.cause: Subscribers land far below 7.5M, so LTV:CAC drops under 1 and $1B content never earns back.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 2M downloads in the first 30 days despite $400M+ marketing

premortem.cause: It repeats Go90: viewership in the thousands per show, advertisers claim make-goods.
premortem.early_signal: App drops out of the US top-50 free chart within 14 days of launch
